question.problem: Given that $r=-2\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta $ for $\theta =\theta (t),$ and that$\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t}=3$ at the point where $\theta =\frac{\pi }{6},$ find $\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}.$
question.worked_solution:
Differentiating the given relation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =-2\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta  \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(r) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-2\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta ) \\ \frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}\theta }(-2\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta ) \\ \frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}\cdot (2{csc}^{2}⁡\theta ).\end{aligned}
$$

Now we can substitute the given information $\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t}=3$ and $\theta =\frac{\pi }{6},$ and solve for $\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}\cdot 2{csc}^{2}⁡\theta  \\ 3 & =\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}\cdot (2{csc}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})) \\ 3 & =\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}\cdot (2\cdot 4) \\ \frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t} & =\frac{3}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$
